documents.unit: Student Handbook / Honor Code (Educational Policy Committee statement on AI)
documents.title: The Honor Code (incl. EPC Policy Statement on AI and Generative AI Statements)
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); AI provision in force since Fall 2023
documents.summary: The Honor Code page embeds the faculty-passed Educational Policy Committee statement: unauthorized AI use in submitted coursework is an Honor Code violation, and permitted use must be acknowledged. It also lists AI-generated content under plagiarism, and gives the Honor Code's sanctions and hearing standard. Instructors are urged to write a syllabus AI policy and use the pledge.
documents.stance_why: The EPC statement says 'Unless explicitly permitted by the instructor, the use of artificial intelligence ... is a violation of the Honor Code', so AI is banned unless an instructor permits it. That is restrict, not delegates, because a university default ban is set and only the exceptions are delegated.

units.why: The sentence sets the default: AI in submitted coursework is banned 'Unless explicitly permitted by the instructor', so the actor is the student, the phase is during-work, modality must-not. P01 fits (default ban) and the misconduct label is coded separately as P36.

units.policy: Unless the instructor explicitly permits it, using artificial intelligence in the production of coursework submitted for evaluation is not allowed.

units.why: Same sentence, second rule: unauthorized AI use 'is a violation of the Honor Code', i.e. it is classified as academic misconduct handled by the honor process. This is P36, not P01, because it states the classification and consequence rather than the default ban; phase when-misuse.

documents.title: Wesleyan University Generative AI Usage Policy
documents.summary: ITS policy for faculty, staff, students and affiliates on using generative AI with university information. It sorts data into Public, Sensitive and Restricted and says which AI tools each may go into, and requires ITS review before AI tools are procured or integrated. It also makes users responsible for checking accuracy and copyright of AI output.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no ban: it states which data classes 'may be entered' into which AI tools, e.g. 'Only information classified as “Public” may be entered into publicly available generative AI tools', so AI use is allowed under data conditions. It says nothing on teaching stance, which it leaves to the honor code.

units.why: 'balance the innovative potential of generative AI with the need to protect sensitive information, uphold academic integrity, and comply with existing laws' states the policy's aim as an institution-wide framework; P56, all, general, informs.
units.anchor: balance the innovative potential of generative AI

units.why: 'This policy is not exhaustive, but represents work towards a thorough and comprehensive policy' says the policy is provisional; P54, all, over-time, informs.
units.anchor: This policy is not exhaustive, but represents work towards a thorough and comprehensive policy.
units.fit_note: States it is incomplete and in progress; no review cycle is named.

units.why: 'applies to all faculty, staff, students, and affiliates ... who collect, use, or share university information in AI tools' sets the scope; P61, all, general, informs.
units.anchor: applies to all faculty, staff, students, and affiliates of Wesleyan University
units.fit_note: Defines scope by persons and information, not a definition of AI.

units.why: 'Users must comply with all relevant Wesleyan University policies' ties AI use to existing policies including academic integrity and the honor code; P77, all, general, must.
units.anchor: Users must comply with all relevant Wesleyan University policies, as well as applicable state and

units.why: 'Only information classified as “Public” may be entered into publicly available generative AI tools' limits what data can go into public AI tools; P50, all, during-work, must-not (for non-Public data).
units.anchor: Only information classified as “Public” may be entered into publicly available generative AI tools

units.why: 'If the tool has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information classified as “Sensitive”' allows Sensitive data only in ITS-approved tools; nearest is P92 (use approved tools), all, may. P50 also fits, but the rule's core is the tool being approved.
units.anchor: If the tool has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information
units.fit_note: Permits Sensitive data in approved tools; framed as a data rule rather than a general duty to use approved tools.

units.why: 'Any information classified as “Restricted” cannot be entered into any generative AI tool without explicit written approval' bars Restricted data absent approval from the CISO and Cabinet member; P50, all, must-not.
units.anchor: cannot be entered into any generative AI tool without explicit written approval
units.fit_note: Also requires named written approvers; P107 (prior approval) was not chosen because the approval concerns data, not AI use generally.

units.why: 'It is the user's responsibility to review the terms and conditions of the software's user agreement before uploading their research information' puts responsibility for terms of use on the user; P114, all, during-work, must.
units.anchor: It is the user’s responsibility to review the terms and conditions of the software’s user
units.fit_note: Covers research uploads and whether the tool trains on supplied data.

units.why: 'users must consult with the university's ITS department to ensure these tools undergo a thorough risk assessment' requires review before procuring AI tools; P65, all, before-course, must.
units.anchor: users must consult with the university's ITS department to ensure these tools undergo a thorough

units.why: Review and approval by ITS is also required for AI that integrates into any Wesleyan system, a distinct scope from procurement; P65, all, before-course, must.
units.anchor: also covers generative AI tools that may integrate into any Wesleyan system, platform, or tool

units.why: 'follow the procurement procedures as outlined in the Vendor Management Policy' sets the procedure for acquiring institutional AI licenses; P65 (review and approval of tools and vendors), all, before-course, should.
units.anchor: If an institutional license is desired, users should follow the procurement procedures
units.fit_note: A procurement procedure rather than a risk review.

units.why: 'AI Generated content may be misleading, fabricated, or false' and 'Users are responsible for verifying the accuracy' tells users to verify output; P31, all, during-work, must.
units.anchor: Users are responsible for verifying the accuracy of content generated by AI tools

units.why: 'ensuring that it does not infringe on copyright' makes users responsible for copyright in AI output, a different rule from accuracy; P52, all, during-work, must.
units.anchor: ensuring that it does not infringe on copyright or contain misleading information

notes: Honor Code page and CFCD page repeat the EPC statement and the Academic Affairs statement; each is coded on its own, so shared units appear in both.
